recent_deploys.message: HOTFIX: disable strict priority field validation in distributor scan to restore job dispatch

ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=f5a9b234 changed the priority column in the job_queue PostgreSQL table from VARCHAR (e.g. high, normal) to INTEGER (e.g. 1, 2), and updated the checkout-service distributor schema validator to expect an integer type. Rows written before the migration retained the old string values while new rows used integers. The strict schema validator in the distributor scan loop failed on every legacy-type row and aborted the entire scan batch, dispatching zero jobs. Rolling back the service to sha=a3f8d120 reversed the validator expectation back to string, but rows written during the window when sha=f5a9b234 was live now contained integers, causing the same strict validation failure in the opposite direction and keeping job dispatch at zero even after rollback.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Hand-deploy hotfix build sha=e92c4f71 which disables strict type-checking on the priority field, allowing the distributor to process rows regardless of column type. 2. Manually scale checkout-service replicas from 3 to 8 to drain the accumulated job backlog of approximately 5900 jobs. 3. Run a data migration to normalize all rows to the new integer type using CASE WHEN priority=high THEN 1 WHEN priority=normal THEN 2 ELSE 3 END. 4. Deploy the permanent fix re-enabling strict integer validation once all rows are homogeneous. 5. Post-incident: enforce backward-compatible multi-phase schema migrations using the expand-contract pattern with schema validation tests run against both old and new row formats before deploy.
